body_text:

Allison Joyce/Bloomberg News



The U.S. added 162,000 jobs in August, the Labor Department reported,  a much-stronger-than-expected result [https://www.wsj.com/economy/jobs/august-jobs-report-unemployment-c9da2f0c] that suggested the labor market shook off its early-summer doldrums.

Below, some of the best analysis and insight from WSJ writers and columnists, the Dow Jones Newswires team and occasionally beyond, on investing, the wealth-management business and more.

Planning & Investing               You’re Not Tough Enough to Earn These Huge Returns

The latest defense of  supercharged ETFs [https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/youre-not-tough-enough-to-earn-these-huge-returns-3feaad7b] doesn’t hold water for most investors.

How to Play the Retirement Tax Guessing Game

Smart retirement-savings strategies [https://www.wsj.com/personal-finance/taxes/how-to-play-the-retirement-tax-guessing-game-e7d31f6d] can save a lot of taxes, if you can take advantage of them.

Market Talk               

From  Dow Jones Newswires [https://www.dowjones.com/professional/newswires/]



The Federal Reserve's decision on whether to raise rates is complicated by the clash of a stable labor market with negative real wage growth, Allianz Investment Management's Charlie Ripley says in a note. The August report's addition of 162,000 jobs reinforces a strong narrative about low growth and low turnover, despite month-to-month volatility, Ripley says. Simultaneously, there's a downward trend in wage growth, which sank to an annual low of 3.09%, he says. Pair that with inflation, and real wage growth is actually negative, Ripley says. Consumers are feeling that squeeze, so raising rates could risk overtightening the economy, he says. August's jobs report shifts September hike expectations sharply, but the outcome is uncertain, Ripley says. (Dean Seal, dean.seal@wsj.com)

The broad consensus among retailers is that consumers are holding up reasonably well, UBS analysts say in a research note. "Yet, that conclusion masks an increasingly nuanced debate," they continue. For starters, consumers' resiliency is closely tied to income level, and "income-based bifurcation has become so widely accepted that it is almost cliche," the analysts say. At the same time, the recent acceleration at dollar stores, coupled with moderation at Walmart and Costco, has prompted renewed questions about shifting consumer behavior. "Investors continue to monitor credit card delinquencies, wealth effects tied to equity markets, and fuel prices as key variables that could shape spending patterns over the next several quarters," the analysts say. (Connor Hart, connor.hart@wsj.com)

Barron's Advisor               IRS Audit-Related Revenue Plunged 35% Last Year. Blame Staff Cuts

The agency’s  examination and collection staff [https://www.barrons.com/advisor/articles/irs-audit-related-revenue-plunged-35-last-year-blame-staff-cuts-fa2c3de1] has shrunk by nearly 36% since fiscal 2024.

Business & Practice               How to Appeal Your Health Insurer’s ‘Prior Authorization’ Denial—and Win

Patients who are denied coverage for a drug or treatment are  often successful when they appeal [https://www.wsj.com/health/healthcare/health-insurance-prior-authorization-denial-appeal-12e1e401], but it takes medical evidence and persistence.

Impact Investing               Big Tech Can Build Data Centers People Won’t Hate

The companies racing to build AI factories are  rethinking their plans [https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/data-center-deals-community-cf92390f] in order to win back the trust of Americans.

Talking Points               This Vintage Printing Press Has Become a Darling of Silicon Valley

Books from Arion Press [https://www.wsj.com/arts-culture/books/arion-press-san-francisco-61ad3948], crafted with lead and tin, can sell for tens of thousands of dollars.

Travel & Lifestyle               The American Dream Is Alive. And It’s Minting Millionaires            

SAVERIO TRUGLIA FOR WSJ



Meet the ‘Everywhere Millionaires’ [https://www.wsj.com/business/entrepreneurship/the-american-dream-is-alive-and-its-minting-millionaires-3903775b] proving that elite degrees aren’t a prerequisite for building massive wealth.

The $400,000 Keys That Get You Into Martha’s Vineyard’s Private Beaches

The island’s coveted ‘beach keys’ are typically kept in the family, but  when they hit the open market [https://www.wsj.com/real-estate/luxury-homes/marthas-vineyard-beach-keys-1897aade], they command big price tags.
